To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) trust, cooperation, and monitoring are interrelated constructs; (b) the relationships between trust and cooperation and between trust and monitoring differ in the two levels of analysis;
the relationships among trust and cooperation and between monitoring and cooperation are moderated by the trustor's and target's perceptions of each other's trust and cooperation.

the relationships among own trust, other's trust, and own cooperation, as well as own monitoring and other's trust are contingent on the level of the interaction (interpersonal or intergroup) and on the level of monitoring (high or low).
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the relationships among trust and cooperation are moderated by monitoring.
understanding the relationships among the three constructs of trust, monitoring, cooperation, and the conditions under which these relationships are likely to be observed.
how trust, monitoring and cooperation are linked in the context of interorganizational relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a very interesting and well written piece of work.
the model provides a more precise and nuanced view of the relationships between trust, monitoring, monitoring and cooperation.
the authors provide a very interesting and novel approach to a very important issue, namely the role of trust in organizations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the authors have developed a model for understanding trust and cooperation that is based on isomorphism and that can be applied to interpersonal as well as intergroup relationships.
we have developed an isomorphic model of trust, monitoring, cooperation, and the relationships among them.

we have provided a more precise definition of the constructs of trust, monitoring, cooperation, and the relationships among them by distinguishing among own and other's constructs and by drawing on the literatures of game theoretic models, interpersonal trust, negotiation, and interorganizatonal relationships.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be more precise in our definitions of the constructs and in our understanding of the relationships among them.
trust, monitoring, cooperation, and their relationships are not the same across levels of analysis.
trust and cooperation are important for the survival of organizations and the individuals within them.
